_comment: What this authority model is enforced by, stated so it is not read as more than it is.

Every action here is checked at three layers on the direct doors (tool schema, dispatch, broker), and the broker's ProcessBackend CONTAINS but does not ISOLATE: pinned cwd, bounded runtime, capped output, credentials stripped from the child environment; neither the filesystem nor the network is confined (governance/broker.py, DEC-010, INV-13).

Known gap until OS isolation lands: test_execute permits running a workspace script, and the script is not governed by this model. It can still read the on-disk .env, write any protected file and open sockets. The verdict is protected against that route (VerificationRunner refuses to grade when a protected file changed since the loop started); the script's other effects are not prevented.
No role may hold 'destructive': it is the action every unmodelled or indirect-execution command grades as, and the fail-closed default depends on no role holding it.
